| Endpoint family | Returns | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| single article | `ArticleRO` | `{ article: {...} }` |
| list | `ArticlesRO` | `{ articles: [...], articlesCount: n }` |
| comments | `CommentsRO` | `{ comments: [...] }` |
| user | `UserRO` | `{ user: {..., token} }` |
| profile | `ProfileRO` | `{ profile: {..., following} }` |

The frontends read `response.article.slug`, `response.user.token`, etc. A method that returns a

text:
**Refined prompt:** Design the delta that gives `Comment` an `author` so comment responses carry the RealWorld spec's `author` profile — answered as a solutioning architect on this TypeORM/NestJS codebase, bound by the existing RO envelope, per-route auth middleware, `synchronize: true` schema management and the LESSONS.md corrections, delivered as a decision table + invariants + impact + numbered open questions + rollout/rollback with no implementation code · **Assumptions:** the target is the TypeORM path on `master` (not `prisma/`), and the scope is the schema+read-path enabler only — the `DELETE` 403 ownership check that `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12` says depends on it is designed here as a seam, not implemented.

---

## The delta in one paragraph

`Comment` (`src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15`) has `id`, `body`, and a `@ManyToOne` to `ArticleEntity`. There is no author column and no relation to `user`, so `CommentsRO` structurally cannot produce the spec's `comment.author`, and `ArticleService.deleteComment()` (`article.service.ts:114-129`) has nothing to compare a caller against. This delta adds one nullable FK, threads the authenticated user id from controller to service on the write path, loads and serializes that author on the read path, and widens the comment response type. It changes no routes, no guard list, and no article response shape.

## Invariants this change must preserve

| # | Invariant | Anchored at |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | Every handler returns its RO envelope; comment bodies stay nested under `@Body('comment')` | LESSONS.md:49-57; `article.controller.ts:77` |
| I2 | Route paths and their order relative to `:slug` are untouched | LESSONS.md:59-66 |
| I3 | The guard list is unchanged: `POST`/`DELETE` comments stay authenticated, `GET /articles/:slug/comments` stays public | `article.module.ts:28-29` vs. absent from lines 23-31 |
| I4 | Layer order controller → service → repository; the controller never touches a repository | every sibling module |
| I5 | `password` never crosses the response boundary | `user.entity.ts:25-26` |
| I6 | Schema changes are additive and nullable — `synchronize: true` with no migration files means the entity *is* the migration and boot must not fail against an existing DB | `ormconfig.json.example:9`; `.claude/knowledge/schema.md:8-9` |
| I7 | `GET /articles/:slug` and `GET /articles` payloads are byte-identical after this change | consequence of D3 |
| I8 | `favoriteCount` / `created` / `updated` naming is not touched here — that is a separate in-flight item | `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9` |

## Decisions

| # | Decision | Rejected alternative | Why it lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Author comes from `@User('id')` as a controller param, passed into `addComment()` as an argument — mirroring `ArticleController.create()` (`article.controller.ts:52`) | Accept `author`/`authorId` from the request body | Trivially forgeable, and LESSONS.md:39-47 already records that the DTO class filters nothing at runtime; no global `ValidationPipe` is registered (`main.ts:5-21`), so the field would reach the entity |
| D1b | — | Read `req.user` inside `ArticleService` | Breaks I4; the service would need the Express request, which no service in this codebase takes |
| D2 | `Comment.author` is a **unidirectional, nullable** `@ManyToOne` → `UserEntity` | Bidirectional with a `UserEntity.comments` `@OneToMany` inverse | Nothing reads comments-by-user; each added non-eager relation is one more property that is `undefined` rather than `[]` (LESSONS.md:68-76). Add the inverse when a feature needs it |
| D2b | — | Denormalize a `authorUsername` string onto `comment` | Goes stale on rename, and the spec's `comment.author` is a full Profile (`bio`, `image`, `following`) — the string cannot produce it |
| D3 | The relation is **not** `eager`; every read path that needs the author declares `relations: ['author']` | `{eager: true}`, which would be a one-line change and need no service edits | `ArticleEntity.comments` is already `{eager: true}` (`article.entity.ts:40`), so this creates a transitive eager chain on all seven `articleRepository.findOne` call sites (`article.service.ts:97,102,115,132,148,166,191`) — and it would drop whole `UserEntity` rows, `password` included, into the `comments` array of every `{article}` response, violating I5 and I7. (It would *not* hit `findAll`/`findFeed`, which use QueryBuilder at lines 28 and 75 — eager applies only to `find*`.) Cost is unbounded, blast radius is every article read |
| D4 | The author is serialized by explicit field construction in a private `ArticleService` builder, mirroring `ProfileService.findProfile()` (`profile.service.ts:35-39`) | `delete comment.author.password`, mirroring `ProfileService.findOne()` (`profile.service.ts:25-26`) | It is a blacklist on a managed entity: any column added to `UserEntity` later leaks by default, and mutating a loaded entity risks writing the hole back if it is ever re-saved |
| D4b | — | `@Exclude()` + `ClassSerializerInterceptor` | No interceptor is registered anywhere (`main.ts:5-21`); adding a global one changes the serialization of every response in the app to fix one field |
| D5 | The author value is the existing `ProfileData` type (`profile.interface.ts:1-6`), imported into `article.interface.ts` | A new `CommentAuthor` type local to the article module | The spec's `comment.author` *is* a Profile; a parallel type guarantees the two drift |
| D6 | `following` is computed against the requesting user, not hardcoded | Always emit `following: false` | This is exactly the failure class in LESSONS.md:95-102 (#99/#45) — a spec field that is present but always wrong renders a permanently-unfollowed author in every RealWorld frontend |
| D7 | `following` is resolved with **one** `followsRepository.find({followerId})` per request, reduced to a set of ids | Per-comment `followsRepository.findOne(...)`, mirroring `profile.service.ts:41` | N+1 on a list endpoint. The batch shape already exists in this very file — `findFeed()` (`article.service.ts:67,73`) — so this mirrors a sibling rather than inventing a pattern |
| D8 | `findComments()` queries `commentRepository` directly (article resolved by slug first) with `relations: ['author']` | Keep routing through `articleRepository.findOne({slug})` with nested `relations: ['comments','comments.author']` | Reloads the whole article plus its eager comment collection just to read comments, and leaves the article-shaped path as a second place that must stay in sync |
| D9 | `addComment()` sets `comment.article` explicitly and persists via `commentRepository.save()` alone | Keep the existing `article.comments.push(comment)` + `articleRepository.save(article)` pair (`article.service.ts:107,110`) and only add the author | Today the insert at line 109 runs with `comment.article` unset and the association is established by the article-side save at line 110 — I did not verify the emitted SQL. That makes the write path depend on the eager collection being loaded, and it is a second write per comment. Setting the owning side directly is the sibling pattern (`FollowsEntity` in `profile.service.ts:65-68`) |
| D10 | `article.interface.ts`'s local `interface Comment` (lines 3-5) is renamed `CommentData` and widened to `{ id, body, author }` | Leave the type alone and let the extra field ride along untyped | It currently declares only `body` — not even `id`, which `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` requires the client to have. The `*RO`/`*Data` types are the client contract (LESSONS.md:49-57), and the name shadows the entity imported as `Comment` elsewhere in the module |
| D11 | `POST` and `DELETE` comment responses keep returning `{article}` (`article.service.ts:111,124`) in this delta | Also fix them to the spec's `{comment}` / empty body now | Bundles a client-breaking response-shape change with a schema change, so rolling back either forces rolling back both. It belongs with the spec-conformance item in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9` |
| D12 | The `DELETE` ownership 403 is **out of scope**; this delta lands only the data it needs | Implement the 403 in the same change | `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12` tracks it as its own item, and it cannot be fully specified until OQ1 is answered — a legacy comment with a NULL author has no defined owner, so the check has no defined verdict |

## Resulting contracts

**Schema delta** — one column on `comment`:

| column | type | null | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `authorId` | int, FK → `user.id` | **yes** (required by I6) | no index specified; see OQ5 |

**`CommentData` after the change** — `{ id: number, body: string, author: ProfileData }`. `CommentsRO` stays `{ comments: CommentData[] }` (I1).

**Signature deltas** (three, all additive):

| Member | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ArticleController.createComment` | `(slug, commentData)` — `article.controller.ts:77` | gains a `@User('id')` param, positioned first to match `create()` at line 52 |
| `ArticleService.addComment` | `(slug, commentData)` — `article.service.ts:101` | gains the author's user id |
| `ArticleController.findComments` / `ArticleService.findComments` | `(slug)` — `article.controller.ts:44`, `article.service.ts:165` | gains the optional current-user id, for D6 |

Note that `findComments` sits on a **public** route (I3), so its `@User('id')` will be `undefined` for anonymous callers — the decorator's unprotected branch (`user.decorator.ts:12-17`) covers this, and `ProfileController.getProfile` (`profile.controller.ts:19`) is the existing precedent for the same pattern on a public route.

## Impact analysis

| Touched | Change | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `comment.entity.ts` | +1 relation | Applied at boot by `synchronize` — see rollback |
| `article.interface.ts:3-5,20-22` | rename + widen `CommentData`; import `ProfileData` | Compile-time only; `CommentsRO`'s envelope name is unchanged |
| `article.service.ts:101-112` (`addComment`) | takes user id; loads the user once; sets both `author` and `article`; drops the article-side save | The one behavioral write change. A user id with no matching row would now write a dangling FK — the middleware already rejects unknown users (`auth.middleware.ts:18-22`), so this is reachable only if the user is deleted mid-request |
| `article.service.ts:165-168` (`findComments`) | reads `commentRepository` with `relations: ['author']`; +1 follows query | Two queries where there was one; both indexed by PK/FK |
| `article.controller.ts:44,77` | +1 param each | — |
| `article.service.ts:114-129` (`deleteComment`) | **unchanged** this delta | Still no ownership check — LESSONS.md:18-27 applies verbatim until D12's follow-on lands |
| `GET /articles`, `GET /articles/:slug`, feed, favorite | **unchanged** (D3 + I7) | Comments continue to serialize as `{id, body}` inside `{article}` — the author appears only via `GET /articles/:slug/comments`. This is an intentional inconsistency; see OQ4 |

**Newly exposed latent bug:** adding `@User('id')` to the public `GET /articles/:slug/comments` routes an expired or tampered token into the unguarded `jwt.verify` at `user.decorator.ts:15`, which throws → **500**, not 401. That is LESSONS.md:29-37 (#79), already live on `GET /profiles/:username` (`profile.controller.ts:19`), but this change adds a second public route to its surface. See OQ3.

**No test coverage exists for this path** — the only spec file in the repo is `src/tag/tag.controller.spec.ts`, so `npm test` will not catch a regression here. Verification is HTTP-level and manual (see rollout).

## Open questions

1. **What happens to comment rows that already exist?** They will have `authorId` NULL, and `comment.author` is non-optional in the spec — frontends read `comment.author.username` and will throw on `null`. Options: backfill to the parent article's author, hard-delete, or serialize a synthetic placeholder profile. *Owner:* whoever owns the deployed database / product. *If unanswered, do not start:* this determines both the serializer's null branch and D12's 403 verdict.
2. **Is there a deployed database with comment rows at all, or is every environment rebuilt from empty?** There are no migrations and no seed script (`package.json:6-14`), which suggests disposable environments — but I have not seen a deploy config. If every environment is disposable, OQ1 is moot and the column can be tightened to `NOT NULL` in a follow-up. *Owner:* whoever owns deploy/ops.
3. **Do we accept the new 500-on-expired-token surface on `GET /articles/:slug/comments`, or is LESSONS.md #79 a prerequisite for this delta?** Fixing it is a ~3-line change in `user.decorator.ts` but widens the diff into the user module. *Owner:* tech lead.
4. **Should `comment.author` also appear in the `comments` array embedded in `{article}` responses?** The spec's article object has no `comments` field at all — ours emits one as a side effect of the eager relation (`article.entity.ts:40`). Suppressing it entirely may be the more spec-correct fix, but that changes an existing payload. *Owner:* whoever owns the spec-conformance item in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9`.
5. **What should happen to a user's comments when the user is deleted?** `DELETE /users/:slug` is public, unauthenticated, and deletes by email (`user.controller.ts:37-40`, `user.service.ts:83-85`). Without an `onDelete` rule the FK behavior is the TypeORM/MySQL default, which I have not verified against this schema. *Owner:* same as OQ1. (Separately: that endpoint being unguarded is its own finding, not part of this delta.)
6. **Do comments need `createdAt`/`updatedAt` in the same change?** The spec's comment object has both; the entity has neither (`comment.entity.ts:5-15`), so comment lists cannot be ordered by age today. Adding them is the same kind of additive column change and could ride along cheaply — or stay with the conformance pass. *Owner:* same as OQ4.

## Rollout

Single deploy, additive, no feature flag — the column is nullable and every new field is on a read path that previously omitted it.

1. Land the entity relation alone (D2) and restart. `synchronize` adds `authorId` as nullable; all responses are unchanged. Confirm boot against a database that already has comment rows.
2. Resolve OQ1 and apply the chosen legacy-row policy before any code reads `comment.author`.
3. Land the interface (D10), service (D1, D7, D8, D9) and controller (D1) changes together — they do not compile independently.
4. Verify by hand, since there is no test for this path: create a comment as user A → `GET /articles/:slug/comments` anonymously (expect `author` present, `following: false`) → repeat authenticated as a user who follows A (expect `following: true`) → confirm the response contains no `password` or `email` key → confirm `GET /articles/:slug` is unchanged from a pre-deploy capture (I7) → replay with an expired token to observe OQ3's behavior.

## Rollback

Reverting the code is safe; reverting the **entity** is not. With `synchronize: true` and no migrations, removing the relation from `comment.entity.ts` and restarting will drop the `authorId` column and every author association written since the deploy — silently, at boot. So:

- **Fast rollback (preferred):** revert only the interface/service/controller commits and leave the relation in place. Responses return to their pre-deploy shape; the column and its data survive, and re-rolling-forward needs no backfill.
- **Full rollback:** only with a database snapshot taken immediately before step 1, and only after accepting the column drop.
- **Irreversible step:** whatever OQ1 resolves to, if it is "hard-delete legacy comments." Take the snapshot before step 2, not before step 3.
